Together Achieving Better
Welcome to Thomas A Becket Junior School
Thank you for visiting our website. We hope you will get a good understanding of what we can offer our children during their time with us. At Thomas A Becket Junior we strive to provide an engaging, creative, stimulating and inclusive learning environment for all of our children to encourage them all to grow and shine in their own unique ways. We hope you will enjoy looking at our website and please feel free to contact us if you would like any further information.
Our Instagram
Year 3 - Start and End Routines and Times from Thursday 3rd September
Thursday 3rd September
Please bring your children to the playground at 9:30am, where they will be met by their class teacher and put into class lines.
Please collect your child at 3:00pm from the class lines on the playground.
Friday 4th September - Wednesday 9th September
Children should arrive and go to their allocated class line space on the playground from 8:30am and will be walked to the class by their teacher at approximately 8:35am - Registers will be taken each morning and close at 8:45am.
The children will be brought to the playground at 3:00pm to be collected.
Thursday 10th September - Friday 11th September
The children should arrive at school between 8:30am and 8:40am and walk straight to their classroom. There will be Year 3 teaching staff and members of the Senior Leadership team at the front of the school and stationed on the route round to the classrooms to direct them where to go. The children should be in class ready for registers to be taken which will close at 8:45am.
The children will be brought to the playground at 3:00pm to be collected.
Monday 14th September onwards
The children should arrive at school between 8:30am and 8:40am and walk straight to their classroom ready for registers to be taken which will close at 8:45am. There will be members of the Senior Leadership team at the front of the school to direct the children if they need it.
The children will be brought to the playground at 3:00pm to be collected.

Clubs
Autumn and Spring Term Enrichment Clubs
The club sign up is now open for Autumn and Spring term clubs.
To ensure we can offer a broad range of clubs across the school year, all sports clubs will run from 3:00 to 3:45pm. This change supports staff availability and recognises that an additional hour of physical activity at the end of the school day can be challenging for some children.
Please see the timetable below for the full list of clubs to be offered in the Autumn and Spring Term.
The closing date to sign-up for all clubs is Tuesday 15th September at 9am.
autumn and spring term clubs 2026.pdf
Please note, many of our clubs are very popular and places cannot be guaranteed for all children that sign-up. Places are randomly selected, this is not done on a "first come, first served" basis.
If you do not receive a confirmation Parentmail by the end of the day on Friday 18th September then unfortunately we have been unable to offer your child a place in the club.
If you have not been successful in gaining a place in the club or if you don't manage to sign up before the closing date we will open a waiting list. If you wish your child to be added to the waiting list for a club, please complete the waiting list google form which will be available on the clubs page on the school website from Monday 21st September.
Clubs are run by our staff on a goodwill basis. To ensure the enjoyment of all, please ensure that your child has a genuine interest in the activity being offered before you book them in. If you require childcare, we have an onsite Childcare Club which runs until 6:00pm. Information about The Childcare Club is available here.
Clubs are due to start during the week commencing 21st September unless otherwise stated.

There are some clubs that are invite only - your child will have received a separate invitation to join this club if it is applicable to them.
Some clubs may be split so that certain year groups will attend for a half-term at a time.
To aid the administration of our clubs, please do not sign your child up for multiple clubs on the same day and the same time.
Children should be collected promptly from the front of the school at the end of the club.
Please remind your child that they are making a commitment and should attend every week.
We would like to remind all families that if your child is unable to attend their scheduled club session, it is your responsibility to inform the school in advance. This helps us ensure the safety and well-being of all children by accounting for their whereabouts during any after-school activities they have been signed up for.
Please notify the school office (or clubs@thomasabecketjunior.org.uk) by 12pm on the day of the club if your child will not be attending.
If your child doesn't attend a club for 2 weeks in a row without notifying us they will be removed from the register and their place offered to another child.
If you have any queries, please email clubs@thomasabecketjunior.org.uk
If children are attending a morning sports club on a non-PE day, they should come to school in their PE kit and change into their school uniform when the club finishes.
If children are attending an after school sports club on a non-PE day, they should come to school in their uniform and change into their PE kit.
For clubs run by external providers, please refer to their communications.

Extra Curricular
Dance at TAB
Dance is a key part of our extra curricular offering at TAB. We take part in a number of events and were even national dance champions two years in a row!
We run different extra curricular dance clubs over the year and also provide the children with the opportunity to take part in dance shows such as ‘Time to Dance’ at the Pavilion Theatre in Worthing and ‘Simply Dance’ with Worthing High School.
These are excellent opportunities for the children to experience dancing on a stage that is regularly used for professional productions and is a real highlight in the school year.
A testament to the impact of this provision for dance is that a number of children return for years after they have left TAB Junior to support with clubs in school and come along to events.
Dance - Extra Curricular
Formula Goblin Go-Kart Club
Formula Goblin Club gives year 6 children the opportunity to build and compete with their very own functioning and drivable electric go-karts.
The karts are assembled from kit-form, where the children split off into various teams to build the chassis, axles, steering mechanism and electrical system. The build introduces children to basic mechanics and, on completion, they have the opportunity to train and compete against other schools from across the country.
The ‘TABinators’ (as the go-karts have been aptly named) may be frequently seen jetting about the school grounds as the children practise and train themselves up for competitions.
Below are some photos of the building process and some of the events we have competed in.
Formula Goblin
Race Report - HMS Excellent, Portsmouth
At our first session of the Formula Goblin Club, Abi P, Louie, Gus, Samuel, Sam and I saw only the chassis of the go-kart built and we carried on the building process from there, in order to have built the TABinator (and have had a few practice drives each) in time for our first competition at the Portsmouth naval base. We all, including Mr Watson, thoroughly enjoyed building and test-driving the Goblin. The week before our first competition in Portsmouth, we had achieved our goal and had completely finished the go-kart.
When we had all arrived at our first competition, we made our final checks of the Goblin: we greased the bearings and, making sure which race was first, slightly let down the tyres for the slalom so that they would have better grip. We pumped them up again for the drag races after we had finished the slalom.
In the slalom, Louie went first, but accidentally missed all the gates, giving him a minute’s penalty, as he went around the wrong cone to begin with. However, we were all proud of him for doing his best; we still had five turns at the slalom and they only take your best score - which Louie got in his second race anyway! After the slalom, we went on to the drag race. We won the majority of our races, and got some fast times; we were all pleased with our performance (Abi P especially as she got the fastest time for our school).
After lunch, we took part in the circuit race, which was the last event. In the circuit race there are three rounds: the heats, the semi-finals and the finals. We all got to vote for who we thought the fastest driver was, so that they could compete in the circuit race - we chose Louie. We were the first team ready for our heat, so got the first pick out of three cards that had the numbers of the lanes on them turned upside-down. Our team picked out the number two, which was the middle lane. We all cheered as loud as we could for him and Louie came in a close second, which meant we didn’t get to move on to the semi-finals, but the Goblin that we came second to was eventually the winner of the entire circuit race, so at least we knew we came second to the best in that race! Sadly, we didn’t win any trophies, but we all had lots of fun and that’s what matters. For our next race in April, we will be practising to get faster and hopefully next time we will bring back some trophies!
Learning an instrument
Learning an instrument is a fun, social activity that we encourage as many children as possible at TAB to be involved in. It can help children to gain confidence, express themselves, gain a new skill and improves memory to help children across their school curriculum. Playing an instrument can also have an incredibly positive impact on children’s mental health. Research has shown that children who play a musical instrument have reduced stress and anxiety, reduced depression and increased self-esteem.
“Not only do you learn a new skill but it opens a part of you that you might not have known before.” Aiofe
“If you learn an instrument it opens up more opportunities.” Erin
“It’s something you can be proud of and show other people.” Lexie
“It’s exciting to learn something and then show your friends.” Eden
“You can express yourself with music.” Molly
“You can learn new songs.” Tia
“If you’re bored it gives you a good thing to do.” Emily

TAB Wheels Up! & Scooter Training
Cycling is a life skill and learning to ride a bike is a rite of passage. Our TAB Wheels Up! programme run by TAB qualified cycle instructors supports children's skills, confidence, and cycling ability through a range of bespoke activities which are adapted to each child’s riding ability.
During the programme TAB Wheels Up! instructors demonstrate how to maintain your bike by checking brakes, steering, handlebars, saddle height, tyre pressure and gears.
Pupils learn the importance of wearing high-visibility clothing and how to check if their helmet fits correctly.
Through our activities, children have the opportunity to learn and develop their cycling ability by completing games where they learn how to look over their shoulder, practice hand signs and develop awareness of speed, stopping distances and bike control.
Pupils complete our obstacle track which teaches them how to control their bikes when using ramps, snaking between poles, manoeuvring around objects and the importance of allowing distance between each rider.
TAB Wheels Up! instructors take pupils onto our school roads where they learn about road skills, observation, hazard awareness and perception of risk.
Riding a bike or scooter to school can improve both physical and mental well-being as well as being a great form of transport, it's also good news for the environment and helps reduce traffic and carbon emissions.

Scooter training
Children undertake a 30 minute session on the school grounds where they learn the key skills of scooting to school safely such as high visibility clothing, respecting pedestrians, safe pavement usage, crossing the road, safe stopping distance, road awareness and scooter control.
Eco-Schools
Following a rigorous application and assessment process we are pleased to announce that Thomas A Becket Junior School is an Eco Schools’ Green Flag Distinction 2026-2027 award holder. Through our continued 'green work' within school and the community we have held this award since 2009, with our application being reviewed every year.
To achieve this award we had to be working on the Eco Schools Framework, by building ‘greenness’ into both the day-to-day life of the school and the children's learning, as well as supporting other schools and organisations to become 'greener' themselves.
Mrs Michelle Mayes, our Sustainability and Forest School Lead, always welcomes support and ideas for the 'green' work that we do. If you would like to be involved in our work, or have ideas to offer, please contact the school office.
Fairtrade Biscuit Bake off
Year 6 pupils impressed us once again this year with their creativity and baking skills during our annual Fairtrade Biscuit Bake Off.
Working in pairs, the pupils researched and designed their own biscuit recipes, aiming to include as many Fairtrade ingredients as possible.
From all the entries, eight teams were selected to bake their biscuits during the school’s Fairtrade Fortnight. The Bake Off was judged by local councillor, Dale Overton, the Chair of the Worthing Fairtrade Group, Rob Thick and Bob Smytherman, along with members of the school community.
With so many tasty biscuits to sample, the judges had a very difficult task deciding on the final winner.
Some pupils from our year 3 Eco Committee attend the Eco Summit at Shoreham Academy. We were joined by other local schools and had the opportunity to participate in three sustainability workshops.
The committee particularly enjoyed drawing and creating pieces of artwork where they had to link nature to the human body.
We all came back to school feeling very inspired by what we had learnt.
We had an amazing opportunity to meet some grey partridge chicks and learn about the challenges these birds face in the wild.
The children discovered that grey partridges are on the Red List of endangered birds in the UK. They learnt that habitat loss and a lack of food in their environment have caused their numbers to decline over time.
Pupils were excited to find out that the chicks they met are part of a local conservation project and will be released back into the wild to help increase the population of this endangered species.
The visit was a fantastic way for children to learn about conservation and the importance of protecting wildlife and their habitats.
Our ducklings have now hatched and this has brought huge eggcitment to the school day! The children have all enjoyed learning about the hatching process over the past few days. Over the next week each class will have the opportunity to spend time with the ducklings and learn more about life cycles and the biology of how eggs grow into ducks.

We were delighted to welcome some hedgehogs to school as part of a special wildlife visit.
The children learnt about the lives of hedgehogs, including what they eat, where they live and how they prepare for hibernation. They also discovered that hedgehog numbers have declined in recent years due to habitat loss, busy roads and a lack of suitable places to shelter.
Pupils were fascinated to see the hedgehogs up close and learnt how they can help protect these much-loved animals by creating wildlife-friendly spaces in their gardens and local areas.
Fascinating Owl Encounter
Year 4 pupils were treated to a memorable and educational experience when the UK Owl & Raptor Centre visited the school.
During the visit, the children had the exciting opportunity to meet three different species of owl: a Long-Eared Owl, a Barn Owl and an Australian Southern Boobook. The visitors shared fascinating facts about each bird, giving pupils a closer look at these remarkable owls and their unique characteristics.
The children learnt about the owls’ natural habitats and discovered where different species live around the world. They also found out what owls like to hunt and watch for when searching for food. The session provided an insight into how these skilled predators survive in the wild.
An important part of the visit focused on conservation. Pupils learnt why the numbers of some owl species are declining, including habitat loss and the use of pesticides. They discovered that pesticides can reduce the number of insects and small mammals that owls rely on for food and in some cases, can harm the birds directly through the food chain. This helped the children understand the importance of protecting wildlife and caring for natural environments.
All members of the Eco-Committee make Reindeer hot chocolate cones in Eco-Club. We used Fairtrade hot chocolate and discuss how purchasing Fairtrade products helps farmers and their communities receive fair pay for their produce.
Fairtrade Award
Recycling at TAB
There are many ways you can recycle your used and unwanted items at TAB.
Our clothes recycling bank is situated near the main entrance. We are able to collect the following items for our clothes bank which helps raise funds for school projects.
We can collect: Clean dry clothing, curtains, household fabrics, bed linen, towels, shoes, handbags etc. Medium size tied bags preferred, with shoes in separate bags.
We cannot collect: Duvets, pillows, cushions, off-cut material, rugs / carpet, wet or soiled clothing and material.
All used batteries can be placed in our battery bank situated in the corridor by the fish tank.
Climate Literacy Accreditation
We are delighted to share that our school has achieved Carbon Literacy status, recognising our commitment to reducing our carbon footprint and taking positive action for the environment.
As part of a national requirement, all schools are required to implement a Climate Action Plan. Our plan outlines the steps we are taking to reduce waste, promote sustainable travel, lower energy use, develop wildlife habitats and engage with our local community
We would also like to congratulate Mrs Mayes, our Sustainability Lead, who has completed her climate literacy training. She will use her knowledge to further enhance our Eco & Fairtrade work, Forest School activities and to enrich environmental and sustainability learning across the curriculum and in extracurricular activities.
School Travel Plan
School Streets Scheme
We are pleased to announce that the School Streets Scheme (TRO, Traffic Regulation Order) has been approved and is running through the school terms. The aim of the scheme is to ensure safer roads around the school making a safer and healthier environment for our children and their parents/carers to walk to school in. This scheme means that during the term time Glebeside Avenue and Glebeside Close are restricted access between 8:00-9:00am and 2:30pm-3:30pm meaning parents/carers are not permitted to be driving into these roads even to just drop off or pick up.

Working in Partnership
As a school we believe it is vital to work in partnership with other schools, educational & community providers. These links support the children's learning as part of the curriculum, in its widest sense, and staff development through learning with, from and on behalf of others.
Locally we work in partnership with:
We also work in partnership with external moderators and other schools to check and validate our assessment judgements.
Our school’s Eco-work as a 'Hall of Fame' School involves supporting other schools (& providers) as they develop their Eco- and FairTrade provision, while the school plays an integral role in the local EYE (Eco, Young & Engaged) Project established by Tim Loughton MP.

Remote Learning
The temporary provisions in the Coronavirus Act 2020 expired on 24 March 2022. As a result the Remote Education (England) Temporary Continuity (No.2) direction no longer has effect.
​Remote education will only ever be considered as a short-term measure and as a last resort where in person attendance is not possible.
In Year 3-6, any home learning will be via Google Classroom. If children are absent due to illness, they are not expected to do home learning.

All online clips sent out for children to use to support their learning will have been vetted by the teachers and will be age appropriate.
For all queries regarding your child’s class please email the class teacher who will reply to your email within 48 hours between 8.00am and 5.30pm Monday to Friday. Teachers' email addresses can be found here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas A Becket Junior School - The ChildCare Club
pageCache.text:
The ChildCare Club
The Childcare Club at Thomas A Becket Junior School offers a breakfast club between 7:40am - 8:40am, and after school care from 3.00pm—6.00pm, on a daily basis, during term time (excluding inset days & bank holidays). The Club is for children who attend the School.
We have been listening to what kids want and combined it with what parents want, which means that the children who attend the club make the choices about what they would like to do and how they would like to do it. Our aim is to widen their experiences and ensure that they are having a great time.
There is a wide and varied choice of equipment allowing for choice, space and time for uninhibited play and areas where children can play. As Play workers, we will facilitate and support the child‘s play; which is based upon observation, reflective practice and base knowledge and understanding of the play process. We also offer structured activities on a daily basis. The children are involved throughout the planning process and we value their ideas and contributions. Help with homework and quiet areas for reading and relaxing are also offered.
The Club is run by a qualified, skilled team of staff in a safe environment and for the kids it’s their own chilled ‘n’ relaxed area. There is always a first aider on-site. All staff have suitable enhanced CRB checks.
If you require any information about The Childcare Club please visit our website http://www.thechildcareclubworthing.co.uk/ or call Harriet Buckingham after 2.30pm on 07818 517618.
NB. The Childcare Club is an independent enterprise not connected to or funded by Thomas A Becket Junior School.

pageCache.text:
Year 3 Admissions September 2026
New Year 3 Intake - Thomas A Becket Junior School September 2026
We are delighted that your child will be joining us in September, and would like to welcome the whole family to our school. We are sure that they will have a happy and enriching time with us and we have a range of activities to help ease the transition from infant school to junior school for all the family.
Year 3 Start and End Routines and Times from Thursday 3rd September
Thursday 3rd September
Please bring your children to the playground at 9:30am, where they will be met by their class teacher and put into class lines.
Please collect your child at 3:00pm from the class lines on the playground.
Friday 4th September - Wednesday 9th September
Children should arrive and go to their allocated class line space on the playground from 8:30am and will be walked to the class by their teacher at approximately 8:35am - Registers will be taken each morning and close at 8:45am.
The children will be brought to the playground at 3:00pm to be collected.
Thursday 10th September - Friday 11th September
The children should arrive at school between 8:30am and 8:40am and walk straight to their classroom. There will be Year 3 teaching staff and members of the Senior Leadership team at the front of the school and stationed on the route round to the classrooms to direct them where to go. The children should be in class ready for registers to be taken which will close at 8:45am.
The children will be brought to the playground at 3:00pm to be collected.
Monday 14th September onwards
The children should arrive at school between 8:30am and 8:40am and walk straight to their classroom ready for registers to be taken which will close at 8:45am. There will be members of the Senior Leadership team at the front of the school to direct the children if they need it.
The children will be brought to the playground at 3:00pm to be collected.
2026 new year 3 intake letter.pdf
School Uniform
Uniform can be purchased from Broadwater Sports or First4Uniform. Please click here to see our school uniform page.
We also have our very own ‘pre-loved’ school uniform shop which is open all year round during term time.
Welcome to Year 3 Presentation and Information
2026 welcome to y3 parents evening presentation.pdf
looking forward to y3 in 26 27.pdf
Meet our Year 3 teachers
//www.youtube.com/embed/HsY1PsQBT90#t=0.5
Free School Meals
The Government gives money to schools to help children from lower income families do their very best. This funding is called 'Pupil Premium'.
This money could be used to help eligible families with the cost of school trips and visits. Children who are registered will also be eligible to receive free hot school meals, saving your approximately £602 per year, should you wish to have them.
Please follow the link below to find out whether your child qualifies and how to apply.
West Sussex County Council - Free School Meals
Hot School Meals
As your child is moving up to year 3, they are unfortunately no longer eligible for universal free school meals.
From September 2026 our hot meals will be delivered by a new provider - ISS Education. They can cater for all dietary needs including religious, vegetarian, vegan and allergies.
ISS will be bringing exciting new menus and a brand new online ordering system to make managing school meals easier than ever for families. Great news on price too, meals will be just £2.95 per day, which is 25p less than the current charge.
More information regarding how to book and order a hot meal for your child will be provided at a later date.
To find out more about what's coming, including menus and how the new ordering system will work, visit www.feedwestsussex.co.uk.
You may also provide your child with a packed lunch if you wish.
School Communications with IRIS ParentMail and IRIS Pay
Communicating with parents is an important part of what we do to ensure you get the correct information about school news and activities.
Thomas A Becket Junior School uses IRIS ParentMail to communicate to parents.
Registering with IRIS ParentMail is very easy. After your child has started with us you will be sent either an email and/or text message from IRIS ParentMail. When you receive this please just follow the instructions in the message.
Once registered, if you have an Android or Apple smartphone, we would highly recommend you download the free IRIS ParentMail App for the best user experience. To do this, simply search for "IRIS ParentMail" in your App store.
When registered you will have access to +Pay on IRIS ParentMail - an online payment service which allows you to pay for school trips/items quickly and easily on your smartphone, tablet or computer.
We will inform you about items you need to pay for through IRIS ParentMail and you will be able to pay electronically, using credit or debit cards, as well as PayPal.
Friends of Thomas A Becket Junior School (FOS)
A warm welcome to Thomas A Becket Junior School to our new families joining the school community, and to existing families with new starters.
Find us on Facebook to keep up to date on events!
FOS - Friends of the School
Clubs
We offer a variety of sport, music and other clubs that run either before school, during lunchtime or after school.
Our club timetable changes in September and after the Easter break.
Clubs that are run by our school staff are free of charge and are run on a goodwill basis. During the first few weeks of the new term in September you will receive a ParentMail with details on how to sign your child up to attend one of our school run clubs.
Please note, many of our clubs are very popular and places cannot be guaranteed for all children that sign up. Places are randomly selected, this is not done on a "first come, first served" basis.
We also have a number of clubs that are run by external providers and there is a charge for these clubs.
Further details can be found on the clubs page on our website here: Clubs
If you require childcare, we have an onsite Childcare Club which runs until 6:00pm. Information about The Childcare Club is available here: The ChildCare Club
